2. Sahani Bibi, the predecessors of the petitioners as the plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of title to 44½ decimals of land of the northern portion of C.S. Plot no. 114 under Khatian No. 124 of Mouza Brahmancharan stating, inter alia, that C.S. Plot No. 112 measuring .53 acre and C.S Plot No. 114 measuring .89 acre of Mouza Brahmancharan were owned by Sk. Mainuddin, who orally sold the same to Chand Bepari at a consideration of Tk. 75/-; Chand Bepari died leaving two sons and 5 daughters; these heirs of Chand Bepari instituted Title Suit No. 167 of 1916 against their co-sharers, Sultan Hossain and others for partition of joint properties, including the aforesaid two plots, in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka; this partition suit was decreed on contest and plaintiffs of that suit got saham which included the aforesaid two Plot Nos. 112 and 114 and the plaintiffs of that suit took possession through Court; by amicable partition Saburunnessa and Jahura Bibi got those two plots in their Saham and sold those two Plots with some other lands to Kari Samiruddin Ahmed by registered sale deed dated 10.04.22 and Kari Samiruddin took possession of his purchased land; Kari Samiruddin. by a registered deed dated 30.05.29 gifted half of the aforesaid Plots to Munshi Md. Nawab Ali who, in his turn, transferred the same to Sarma Sundari Guha by registered sale deed dated 05.01.30; by amicable partition amongst the co-shares, Sarma Sundari Guha got the northern portion of the Plot Nos. 112 and 114 and subsequently sold the same to Rdmjan Ali by registered deed of sale dated 08.12.38; Ramjan Ali died leaving wife Faizun Nessa Bibi, 5 sons Abbas Ali, Ahmed Ali, Ansar, Abdur Razzak and Md. Giasuddin and two daughters, Amena Khatun and Sahera Khatun; 34 acre of Plot No. 114 was recorded in the name of Faizunnessa in the State Acquisition Khatian as Plot No. 473 and .37 acre of Plot No. 114 was recorded in the name of Shamsuddin Mia (who purchased from Asahuddin Mia purchaser from heir of Md. Nowab Ali Mia) and the remaining 18 decimals of the said Plot was recorded in the name of Province of East Pakistan in the khan Khatian No. 1; all the heirs of said Ramjan Ali transferred 31½ decimals of land to Sahani Bibi. predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners and 13 decimal of land to Md. Son Mia from Plot No. 114 by two separate sale deeds dated 16.02.65 and the purchasers were given possession in their respective land; Md. Sona Mia subsequently. transferred his 13 decimals of land to Sahani Bibi by registered sale deed dated 12.11.66 and put her in possession of the same Sahani Bibi. predecessors-in-interest of the petitioners, thus acquired total 441/2, decimals of land in the northern portion of C.S. Plot No. 114 and got her name mutated in the' S.A Khatian in place or Faizunnessa (wile of Ramjan Ali) and others in respect of 34 decimals and mutation of 10½ decimals was done through Court by a proceeding under section I 43A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act; Sahani Bibi paid rent in respect of the said land upto 1983; Sabani Bibi has been in possession all along cultivating land through laborers and growing cauli flowers and paddy etc. therein and R.S. record was prepared in her name; defendants claimed title to the suit land as grand children of Sk. Moinuddin (defendant of Title Suit No. 167 of 1916) and got the R.S. record changed in their names; such action having clouded the title of the plaintiff (Sabani Bibi) she was constrained to institute the suit. 

 3. The successive heirs of Sk. Moinuddin, defendants nos. 1-9 contested the suit by filing one written statement and the added defendant Nos. 10-18 (who purchased some interest from the heirs of Sk. Moinuddin) contested by filing a separate written statement. It was contended by defendant Nos. 1-9, inter alia, that the suit property was owned by Sk. Moinuddin and his name was correctly recorded in the C. S. record of right. Sk. Moinuddin possessed the suit proper) by constructing but there son and cultivating portion of land. Ile died leaving behind two sons. Abdus Sattar and Abdul Halim. There was no partition of the suit property amongst the co-shares of Chand Bapari and possession was not taken through Court by decree-holder; deed of gift in favour of Md. Nowab Ali in respect of 2 decimals of land of Plot No. 114 in favour of Sarma Sundari Guha is false. Ramjan Ali did not acquire any title by purchase from Sunlit Sundari Guha; the suit land was vacant nal/land and remained under water most of the year; the suit land had been in possession of the defendants from the time of their predecessor-in-interest and the same stood recorded in their names in the S.A. and revisional settlement Khatian and rent had been paid by them in respect of .the suit land; defendant Nos. 1-9 are heirs and successors-in-interest of Abdul and Abdus Sattar sons of Sk. Moinuddin, the plaintiff Sahani Bibi has got no title to or interest in the suit land and her deeds of title are collusive and without consideration. 

 5. Mr. Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that no issue having been raised by the defendants as to identity of the suit land in their written statement and the point having been urged for the first time at the time of hearing argument in the suit and the plaintiff appellant even, at that time prayed for holding local investigation for settling the question as to identity of the suit land which was rejected; the trail Court seriously erred in law in holding that from the description of the land in Ext. I (plaint in Title Suit No. 167 of 1916) as shown by boundary it was not possible to ascertain whether the schedule of Ext.1 attracted suit plot No. 114 and no attempt was made on the side of the plaintiff to prove the identity of the suit land with reference to the schedule of Ext. 1 and High Court Division erred in affirming such finding of the learned trial Court. The learned Counsel next submits that in view of the final decree in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiff in Partition suit No. 167 of 1916 and successive transfers from 1922 of the land of the suit Plot No. 114 under C.S. Khatian No. 124 of Mouza Brahmanchiran, evidenced by Exhibits 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 and mutation of the names of Sahani Bibi plaintiff in respect of 34 acre through proceeding; before the revenue officer and in respect of 10½ decimal (wrongly recorded in the names of Government) by proceeding under section 143 A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the rent receipts Ext. 13, 13(a) and 13(h) all subsequent to the C.S. record of right Ext. A in the name of Mainuddin Kochwan, High Court Division erred in law in holding (without considering all these evidence) that the presumption of Ext. A had not been rebutted. Ile next submits that the trial Court as also the High Court Division misconstrued transfer document Ext. 5 reading –প্রকাশ থাকে যে, ৬নং তফসিলে নাল জমি ষোল আনা দীর্ঘকাল যাবৎ আমার খাস দখলে আছে উহার হিস্যা। আট আনা উত্তরাংেশের অত্র দলিল মূলে আপনার দখলে অর্পন করিলাম ও আপনার খাস দখলে বুঝাইয়া দিলাম।  and erred in concluding  that the transfer was only of .02 acre of the suit plot inasmuch as item 6 of the schedule of that document related to Plot No. 114 under Khatian No. 124 of Mouza Brahmanchiian, northern hall of which amounted to. 44½, acre. The learned Counsel next submits that a reading of the evidence of the P. Ws. shows that there was no contradiction in their evidence as found by the High Court Division and their evidences were consistent on the point that the plaintiff was in possession by producing cauli flower pumpkin etc. through borgadar P.W. 3 and such possession of the plaintiff is consistent with the averments made by the defendant Nos. 1-9 in their written statements in paragraph 18(3) together with the evidence of D.W. 6, Md. Shaljahan son of Kamrunnessa (defendant No. 9) that they possessed in the southern part of the suit plot. The learned Counsel lastly submits that in view of the long lapse of time from the decree Ext. 2 and the evidence of possession on record, the High Court Division erred in law in delving into question of the decree Ext. 2 being nullity giving no title to Saburunnessa and Juhura Bibi on the ground that minor sons of Mainuddin Kochwan not being properly represented by Court guardian and transfers made by the heirs of Abdul Halim as late as in 1981 during the pendency of the suit.
